subject: Discovery recap: Reliability & graceful degradation for AcmeAI

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwoodinference.com>

Cc: Chloe Martin <chloe.martin@redwoodinference.com>

Subject: Discovery recap: Reliability & graceful degradation for AcmeAI

Hi Sarah — great to meet today, thanks for the time. Quick recap from our discovery call and proposed next steps so we stay aligned. Please reply with any corrections or additions.

Key pain points you shared
- Recent production incidents (Sept + Oct) caused multi-minute latency spikes and two partial outages for your inference service.
- No consistent automated fallback: when the primary model node pool exhausted capacity you currently return 503s or queue requests.
- High sensitivity to tail latency for user-facing flows (chat/assist) — customers notice when responses exceed ~500ms.
- Compliance & audit needs: SOC 2 evidence and incident timelines are required for your board review.

Current stack you mentioned
- Self-hosted model proxy on AWS (us-east-1), custom autoscaling for inference nodes.
- Mix of open models + some fine-tuned variants.
- Long tail of token costs due to repeated cold KV cache warming across many tenants.

Success criteria you outlined
- 95th/99th latency targets: 95th < 300ms, 99th < 800ms for common user flows.
- Availability target: move from ~99.9% to 99.95%+ for inference endpoints.
- Graceful degradation behavior: when capacity is constrained, return degraded-but-useful responses (smaller model / condensed output) rather than errors.

Suggested Redwood approach / capabilities
- Multi-tier serving: automatic fallbacks to quantized/optimized model variants when primary capacity is constrained.
- Region-aware routing: failover to secondary region (us-west-2) with cached prefix responses for critical paths.
- Prefix/KV caching and workload-aware batching to reduce cost and lower token latency for repeated prompts.
- SLA options: Dedicated capacity plan with 99.95% availability + credits; hosted options for proof-of-concept.

Immediate next steps
1) I will share a short mutual action plan (MAP) and a proposed workshop agenda for a technical deep dive. (attached MAP-AcmeAI-20261101.pdf)
2) Please send the SOC 2 questionnaire and any incident reports you can share — we'll have our security team start a review.
3) Proposal: 60-minute technical workshop w/ your infra + our SRE/Servicing engineer. Are you available Nov 5 or Nov 6?

Attachments: MAP-AcmeAI-20261101.pdf

Thanks — I'll loop Marissa (solutions lead) and Chloe (customer success) on next steps.

Best,
Ben Carter

Hi Sarah — thanks for the details and the attachments. Quick responses below, plus proposed next steps.

Graceful degradation capabilities
- Model-variant fallback: Redwood can route to a smaller quantized variant automatically when primary pools are overloaded; responses are shortened but remain coherent. We track quality with prompt-based checks and can configure thresholds per route.
- Cache-backed degraded responses: for a set of critical prompts we can serve cached condensed responses when model latency exceeds a threshold. This reduces exposure during cold-warm cache events.
- Observability: tracing and token-level latency breakdowns so you can audit when fallbacks happen.

Region failover implications
- Failover to a secondary region will add cross-region latency for the first redirected requests; for active sessions we recommend sticky routing + replicated caches for critical flows to minimize user impact. We can run a workshop to map which flows need strict session affinity.

SLA / pricing (indicative)
- Dedicated capacity tier: 99.95% availability SLA with service credits; suitable for your production-critical endpoints.
- Hosted (managed) tier: lower commit + higher variance in tail latency, no 99.95 SLA.
- Pricing: rough estimate -> Dedicated starts at ~3\u20135x hosted for the same qps profile (dependent on model footprints, quantization). We\u2019ll provide a formal quote after the workshop.

Next steps
1) Technical workshop: Nov 5, 10:00 AM ET — confirm? Attendees: your infra lead + product, our SRE (Marissa) + solutions engineer (Chloe).
2) I\u2019ll have our security team follow up on the SOC 2 questionnaire within 48 hours.
3) We\u2019ll draft a tailored MAP and preliminary SLA language for review. HubSpot deal created: https://app.hubspot.com/deals/1234567890

Attached: MAP-AcmeAI-20261101.pdf (high-level milestones and responsibilities).

Cheers,
